previous_verdict.blocking_finding: Pantry identities were unconstrained String values, and real-device completion accepted non-UUID IDs rice and stock.

reviewed_commits.subject: feat(data): add local kitchen and cooking records

gap_resolution.implementation: PantryItemId is a private-constructor data class. Its only normal construction path parses java.util.UUID, requires the caller text to equal the canonical representation ignoring case, and stores the canonical lowercase representation.
gap_resolution.typed_surface: PantryItemEntity.id, PantryBinding.pantryItemId, ActualPantryUse.pantryItemId, PantryRemaining.pantryItemId, CompletionResult identity payloads, PantryDao.get, InventoryCompletionDao.pantryRows, Room columns, and JSON fields all use PantryItemId.
gap_resolution.minimality: One value type and two direct Room converter methods close the boundary without a factory, interface, dependency, or speculative layer. @ConsistentCopyVisibility keeps the generated data-class copy path private with the constructor.
gap_resolution.room_json_safety: Room generated code serializes PantryItemId through pantryItemIdToString and parses result rows through stringToPantryItemId; completion remains wrapped by RoomDatabaseKt.withTransaction. JSON writes canonical id.value and every read calls requiredPantryItemId, so malformed persisted JSON fails closed before producing a domain object.

requirements_verified.canonical_uuid_before_domain_and_storage: pass: malformed, shortened, empty, and leading-space forms parse to null; arbitrary String IDs cannot be supplied to entity/binding/use/DAO constructors.
requirements_verified.uppercase_normalization: pass: uppercase canonical input stores lowercase; fresh JShell showed uppercase and lowercase inputs produce equal values, equal hashes, and one HashSet identity.
requirements_verified.malformed_uuid_no_mutation: pass: targeted real-Room regression asserted all three malformed parses are null while complete pantry rows and meal-log count remain unchanged.
requirements_verified.valid_unknown_uuid: pass: targeted regression returns UnknownInventory with the exact typed valid UUID and leaves both pantry rows and log count unchanged.
requirements_verified.duplicate_uuid: pass: targeted regression returns DuplicateInventoryId with the exact typed UUID before mutation; canonical case normalization makes case variants the same key.
requirements_verified.version_unit_binding: pass: completion compares source version and unit with both immutable recipe binding and the row reread inside the transaction.
requirements_verified.parser: pass: strict g, ml, count and signed Long milli-unit parsing behavior remains covered, including at most three decimal places and overflow rejection.
requirements_verified.persistence_and_snapshot: pass: file Room database close/reopen retains exact inventory and serialized immutable meal snapshot.
requirements_verified.zero_row: pass: fresh SM_F711N test retains the zero-quantity stock row and two total pantry rows.
requirements_verified.rollback: pass: over-use, unit mismatch, stale version, duplicate typed UUID, and unknown typed UUID leave all pantry rows and meal-log count unchanged.
requirements_verified.concurrency: pass: fresh SM_F711N test ran three iterations; every iteration asserted exactly one Success, one StaleInventory, remaining quantity 9000, and one meal log.

residual_risks: PantryBindings still permits duplicate already-canonical IDs and complete uses associateBy, so malformed snapshot construction could silently choose the last binding. Current recipe/backend validation is expected to prevent this, but a local uniqueness invariant would be safer before wider import/migration surfaces exist.

Inventory version increment remains unchecked at Int.MAX_VALUE and can wrap. This is outside the UUID fix and not reachable through current creation flows, but should be guarded if imported/corrupt data becomes in scope.

Database version remains 1 after changing the physical ID converter contract. No pantry UI or released user data exists at T2, so current clean-install verification is valid; a future migration gate must explicitly cover any pre-fix development database retention expectation.
